2063-the-trail-of-the-white-mule.description: A book by B. M. Bower. "Better go put up your bail and then forfeit it," he advised in a milder tone. "The judge will probably remember you; I do, and my memory ain't the best in the world. Twice you've been hooked for speeding through traffic; and parking by fire-plugs and in front of the No Park signs and after four, seems to be your big outdoor sport. Forfeit your bail, old boy--or it's thirty days for you, sure."

arxiv-2101-07612.title: Comparative Evaluation of 3D and 2D Deep Learning Techniques for Semantic Segmentation in CT Scans
arxiv-2101-07612.creator: Abhishek Shivdeo, Rohit Lokwani, Viraj Kulkarni, Amit Kharat, Aniruddha Pant
arxiv-2101-07612.description: Abstract Image segmentation plays a pivotal role in several medical-imaging applications by assisting the segmentation of the regions of interest. Deep learning-based approaches have been widely adopted for semantic segmentation of medical data. In recent years, in addition to 2D deep learning architectures, 3D architectures have been employed as the predictive algorithms for 3D medical image data.

arxiv-2103-12223.title: Analysis and control of agreement and disagreement opinion cascades Thanks: This research has been supported in part by NSF grant CMMI-1635056, ONR grant N00014-19-1-2556, ARO grant W911NF-18-1-0325, DGAPA-UNAM PAPIIT grant IN102420, Conacyt grant A1-S-10610, and by NSF Graduate Research Fellowship
arxiv-2103-12223.creator: Alessio Franci, Anastasia Bizyaeva, Shinkyu Park, Naomi Ehrich Leonard
arxiv-2103-12223.description: Abstract We introduce and analyze a continuous time and state-space model of opinion cascades on networks of large numbers of agents that form opinions about two or more options. By leveraging our recent results on the emergence of agreement and disagreement states, we introduce novel tools to analyze and control agreement and disagreement opinion cascades.

arxiv-2405-18662.title: Understanding Intrinsic Socioeconomic Biases in Large Language Models
arxiv-2405-18662.creator: Mina Arzaghi, Florian Carichon, Golnoosh Farnadi
arxiv-2405-18662.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into critical decision-making processes, such as loan approvals and visa applications, where inherent biases can lead to discriminatory outcomes. In this paper, we examine the nuanced relationship between demographic attributes and socioeconomic biases in LLMs, a crucial yet understudied area of fairness in LLMs.

arxiv-2407-00841.title: Short-term stability of a microcell optical reference based on Rb atom two-photon transition at 778 nm
arxiv-2407-00841.creator: Martin Callejo 1, Andrei Mursa 1, Rémy Vicarini 1, Emmanuel Klinger 1, Quentin Tanguy 1, Jacques Millo 1, Nicolas Passilly 1, Rodolphe Boudot 1
arxiv-2407-00841.description: Abstract We report on the development and short-term stability characterization of an optical frequency reference based on the spectroscopy of the rubidium two-photon transition at 778 nm in a microfabricated vapor cell. When compared against a 778 nm reference signal extracted from a frequency-doubled cavity-stabilized telecom laser, the short-term stability of the microcell frequency standard is 3.

arxiv-2408-15291.title: A temperature scale of 1 ∼ \sim 2 eV in the mass-radius relationship of white dwarfs of type DA Journal: New Astronomy
arxiv-2408-15291.creator: Jin Lim, Ji-Yu Kim, Maurice H.P.M. van Putten
arxiv-2408-15291.description: Abstract The mass-radius relationship of white dwarfs (WDs) is one of their defining characteristics, largely derived from electron degeneracy pressure. We present a model-independent study of the observed mass-radius relationship in WD binaries of Parsons et al. 2017 , listing data over a broad temperature range up to about 60,000 K (5 eV).

arxiv-2410-02164.title: Universality in Transfer Learning for Linear Models
arxiv-2410-02164.creator: Reza Ghane, Danil Akhtiamov, Babak Hassibi
arxiv-2410-02164.description: Abstract We study the problem of transfer learning and fine-tuning in linear models for both regression and binary classification. In particular, we consider the use of stochastic gradient descent (SGD) on a linear model initialized with pretrained weights and using a small training data set from the target distribution.

pmc-11478945.title: Research on a 3D Point Cloud Map Learning Algorithm Based on Point Normal Constraints
pmc-11478945.creator: Zhao Fang, Youyu Liu, Lijin Xu, Mahamudul Hasan Shahed, Liping Shi, Roberto Teti, Peng Cao, Junxing Zheng
pmc-11478945.description: Laser point clouds are commonly affected by Gaussian and Laplace noise, resulting in decreased accuracy in subsequent surface reconstruction and visualization processes. However, existing point cloud denoising algorithms often overlook the local consistency and density of the point cloud normal vector. A feature map learning algorithm which integrates point normal constraints, Dirichlet energy, and coupled orthogonality bias terms is proposed.

pmc-11497177.title: Surgical resection and overall survival in cT4b sinonasal non‐squamous cell carcinoma
pmc-11497177.creator: Aman M. Patel, Afash Haleem, Lucy Revercomb, Jason A. Brant, Michael A. Kohanski, Nithin D. Adappa, James N. Palmer, Jennifer E. Douglas, Ryan M. Carey
pmc-11497177.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). ObjectiveSurgical resection is associated with higher overall survival (OS) than definitive radiotherapy (RT) or chemoradiotherapy (CRT) in cT4b sinonasal squamous cell carcinoma (SCC). Our study investigates the survival benefit of surgical resection in cT4b sinonasal non‐SCC.MethodsThe 2004 to 2019 National Cancer Database was queried for patients with cT4b sinonasal non‐SCC undergoing definitive treatment with (1) surgical resection + additional therapy (RT, chemotherapy, or both), (2) RT alone, or (3) CRT.

pmc-12591791.creator: Xinyi Chai, Wei Yang, Qiang Gao, Fangtong Zhu, Yingjie Cai, Xiaojiao Peng, Ping Yang, Jiashu Chen, Xin Ni, Ming Ge
pmc-12591791.description: BackgroundFractal dimension (FD) analysis of preoperative magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans offers a potential approach to quantify tumor structural complexity, but its utility for predicting tumor grade and cerebellar mutism syndrome (CMS) risk in pediatric posterior fossa tumors remains unestablished.

pmc-12780261.description: Large public datasets of the human microbiome now exist but combining them for large-scale analysis is difficult due to a lack of standardization. We developed curatedMetagenomicData (cMD) 3, a uniformly processed collection of over 22,000 human microbiome samples with manually curated metadata from 94 studies and 42 countries.

pmc-13196759.title: Evolution of a central dopamine circuit underlies adaptation of a light-evoked sensorimotor response in the blind cavefish
pmc-13196759.creator: Robert A. Kozol, Ally Canavan, Bernadeth Tolentino, Alex C. Keene, Johanna E. Kowalko, Erik R. Duboué
pmc-13196759.description: Adaptive behaviors emerge in novel environments through functional changes in neural circuits. While relationships between circuit function and behavior are well studied, how evolution shapes circuits to drive behavioral adaptation is poorly understood. The Mexican cavefish, Astyanax mexicanus, provides a unique genetically tractable model, with above ground eyed surface fish and multiple blind cavefish populations that have evolved in darkness.
